# Forge

> Compile-time object mapping for C# powered by Roslyn source generators. Zero runtime reflection, zero allocation overhead, hand-written-code performance.

Forge generates partial method bodies at compile time that map properties between source and destination types. You decorate a static partial class with `[Forge]`, declare partial method signatures, and the source generator writes the implementations. An accompanying Roslyn analyzer emits 87 diagnostics (FKF001–FKF807) to catch mistakes at build time.

## Installation

```xml
<PackageReference Include="FreakyKit.Forge.Generator" Version="1.5.0" />
<PackageReference Include="FreakyKit.Forge.Analyzers" Version="1.5.0" />
```

Both pull in `FreakyKit.Forge` (core attributes) transitively.

## Core Concepts

**Forge class** — a `static partial class` decorated with `[Forge]`. Contains forge method declarations.
**Forge method** — a `static partial` method whose body the generator writes. Two shapes:
- **Create**: one parameter (source), returns destination type.
- **Update**: two parameters (source, existing destination), returns void.

**Member matching** — properties matched by name (case-insensitive). Fields included only with `ShouldIncludeFields = true`.

**Type mismatch resolution chain** (in order): nullable handling, enum mapping, enum-string mapping, dictionary mapping, collection mapping, type converters (`[ForgeConverter]`), implicit numeric conversions, nested forging (`AllowNestedForging = true`), then error FKF200.

## Attributes

### `[Forge]` — class-level
| Property | Type | Default | Purpose |
|----------|------|---------|---------|
| `Mode` | `ForgeMode` | `Implicit` | `Implicit`: all shaped methods are forged. `Explicit`: only `[ForgeMethod]`-decorated ones. |
| `ShouldIncludePrivate` | `bool` | `false` | Include private forge methods. |
| `GenerateExtensionMethods` | `bool` | `true` | Emit extension method class for `source.ToDto()` syntax. |

### `[ForgeUses(params Type[])]` — class-level
Declares other `[Forge]` classes whose methods are searched during nested forge/converter/condition resolution. Order matters — first match wins.

### `[ForgeIncludes(params Type[])]` — class-level
Inherits property assignments from included `[Forge]` classes. When a forge method maps `DerivedSource → DerivedDto` and an included class has a method mapping `BaseSource → BaseDto` (where derived types extend base types), the base assignments are inlined into the derived method. Local assignments take precedence. Unlike `[ForgeUses]` (method discovery for nested forging), `[ForgeIncludes]` copies base-type property mappings directly. Diagnostics: FKF533 (not found), FKF534 (not forge), FKF535 (circular), FKF536 (no compatible method), FKF537 (shadowed), FKF538 (missing [Forge]).

### `[ForgeMethod]` — method-level
| Property | Type | Default | Purpose |
|----------|------|---------|---------|
| `ShouldIncludeFields` | `bool` | `false` | Map public fields alongside properties. |
| `AllowNestedForging` | `bool` | `false` | Call other forge methods for type-mismatched members. |
| `MappingStrategy` | `ForgeMapping` | `Cast` | Enum mapping: `Cast` (direct cast) or `ByName` (switch by name). |
| `AllowFlattening` | `bool` | `false` | Flatten nested source paths into flat destination members (`AddressCity` from `Address.City`). |
| `GenerateExpression` | `bool` | `false` | Emit `Expression<Func<TSource,TDest>>` for EF Core `IQueryable.Select()`. |
| `IgnoreIfNull` | `ForgePolicy` | `Inherit` | Wrap all assignments in null checks. |
| `StrictMapping` | `bool` | `false` | Unmapped members become errors instead of warnings. |
| `ShareReference` | `ForgePolicy` | `Inherit` | Reference-share same-type mutable collections instead of deep-copying. |

### `[ForgeMap("name")]` — property/field/ctor-parameter level
Maps to a differently-named counterpart member.
| Property | Type | Default | Purpose |
|----------|------|---------|---------|
| `DefaultValue` | `object?` | `null` | Fallback for `Nullable<T>` to `T` mappings. |
| `IgnoreIfNull` | `ForgePolicy` | `Inherit` | Per-member null-check override. |
| `IgnoreIfDefault` | `bool` | `false` | Skip assignment when source equals `default(T)`. |
| `Condition` | `string?` | `null` | Name of a static `bool Method(SourceType)` — skip assignment when false. |
| `ShareReference` | `ForgePolicy` | `Inherit` | Per-member collection reference-sharing override. |
| `NullFallback` | `NullFallback` | `Null` | What to do when source is null during nested forging: `Null` or `DefaultConstruct`. |

### `[ForgeIgnore]` — property/field level
Exclude from mapping. Optional `Side` property: `Both` (default), `Source`, `Destination`.

### `[ForgeConverter]` — method-level
Marks a static method as a type converter. Must be static, non-void, non-generic, one parameter.

### `[ForgePolymorphic(Type, string)]` — method-level (AllowMultiple)
Declares a polymorphic dispatch arm. The method generates a switch expression dispatching to other forge methods by runtime type. Pure dispatch — no property mapping. Default arm throws `InvalidOperationException`. Non-default `[ForgeMethod]` options emit FKF804; `GenerateExpression = true` emits FKF805. Diagnostics: FKF800-FKF807.

### `[ForgeDictionary]` — method-level
Controls dictionary mapping behavior.
| Property | Type | Default | Purpose |
|----------|------|---------|---------|
| `KeyCasing` | `KeyCasingPolicy` | `Exact` | `Exact`, `IgnoreCase`, `CamelCase`, `SnakeCase`. |
| `MissingKey` | `MissingKeyPolicy` | `Throw` | `Throw`, `UseDefault`, `Skip`, `ReturnNull`. |
| `NullValue` | `NullValuePolicy` | `Include` | `Include`, `Skip`. |

## Enums

| Enum | Values |
|------|--------|
| `ForgeMode` | `Implicit` (0), `Explicit` (1) |
| `ForgeMapping` | `Cast` (0), `ByName` (1) |
| `ForgePolicy` | `Inherit` (0), `True` (1), `False` (2) |
| `ForgeIgnoreSide` | `Both` (0), `Source` (1), `Destination` (2) |
| `NullFallback` | `Null` (0), `DefaultConstruct` (1) |
| `KeyCasingPolicy` | `Exact`, `IgnoreCase`, `CamelCase`, `SnakeCase` |
| `MissingKeyPolicy` | `Throw`, `UseDefault`, `Skip`, `ReturnNull` |
| `NullValuePolicy` | `Include`, `Skip` |

## Method Shapes

```csharp
// Create — one param, returns destination
public static partial PersonDto ToDto(Person source);

// Update — two params, void return, modifies existing object
public static partial void Update(Person source, PersonDto existing);

// Collection projection — both param and return are collections
public static partial List<PersonDto>? ToDtos(List<Person>? source);
```

## Constructor Selection

1. Public parameterless constructor (preferred).
2. Public parameterized constructor where every parameter matches a source member by name+type.
3. No construction in update mode.
Errors: FKF500 (ambiguity), FKF501 (missing param), FKF502 (no viable ctor), FKF503 (abstract/interface/static).

## Init-Only Properties

Properties with `init` setters go into an object initializer block. In update methods they are skipped (cannot be reassigned).

## Flattening

With `AllowFlattening = true`, unmatched destination members are matched by decomposing their name as a prefix chain: `AddressCoordsLatitude` matches `source.Address?.Coords?.Latitude`. Null-conditional operators inserted automatically for reference-type intermediates. Max depth: 10 levels. Only properties are traversed (not fields).

## Nested Forging

With `AllowNestedForging = true`, type-mismatched members are converted by calling another forge method in the same class (or included via `[ForgeUses]`). Null-safe: `source.X != null ? Convert(source.X) : null`.

## Collection Mapping

Supports `List<T>`, `T[]`, `HashSet<T>`, `IEnumerable<T>`, `ImmutableArray<T>`, `ImmutableList<T>`, `ReadOnlyCollection<T>`, `Collection<T>`, and interface forms. Different element types use `.Select(x => ForgeMethod(x))` with appropriate materializer.

## Same-Type Collection Semantics

Default: **deep-copy** (`new List<T>(source.X)`). Opt into reference-sharing with `ShareReference = ForgePolicy.True`. Precedence: destination-side `[ForgeMap]` > source-side `[ForgeMap]` > method-level `[ForgeMethod]` > default (False/deep-copy). Immutable collections always direct-assign. Same-type custom classes always reference-share (FKF312).

## Enum-String Mapping

- Enum to string: `source.Status.ToString()`
- String to enum: `Enum.Parse<T>(source.Status)`
- With fallback: `[ForgeMap("Status", DefaultValue = Status.Unknown)]` uses `Enum.TryParse` with fallback value.

## Dictionary Mapping

Supports `Dictionary<string, object>` and `Dictionary<string, string>` as source/destination. String values parsed via `int.Parse()`, `bool.Parse()`, `Enum.Parse<T>()`, etc. Configure with `[ForgeDictionary]` attribute for key casing, missing key handling, and null value filtering.

## Expression Projections (EF Core)

`GenerateExpression = true` emits `Expression<Func<TSource, TDest>>` for `IQueryable.Select()`. Requires EF Core 8+. Nested forge methods are inlined (no `Expression.Invoke`). Members with `IgnoreIfNull`, `IgnoreIfDefault`, `Condition`, `[ForgeConverter]`, or non-translatable collection materializers are silently omitted (FKF506). Update methods cannot have expressions (FKF504). Cycle detection via FKF507. Depth warning at 4+ levels (FKF508), error at 7+ (FKF509).

## Before/After Hooks

Convention-based partial methods:
- `static partial void OnBefore{MethodName}({SourceType} source)` — called before assignments.
- `static partial void OnAfter{MethodName}({SourceType} source, {DestType} result)` — called after assignments.

## Extension Methods

Default on. Generates `{ForgeClass}Extensions` with `this` overloads. Disabled for nested classes. Set `GenerateExtensionMethods = false` to suppress.

## Error Handling

Error-severity diagnostics block generation for the entire forge class. No partial output. All errors collected before stopping.

## Code Fix Providers (Lightbulb Suggestions)

Forge ships code fix providers alongside the analyzer. When a diagnostic fires in the IDE, a lightbulb offers an automatic fix:

| Diagnostic | Fix |
|---|---|
| FKF003 (class not static) | Add `static` modifier |
| FKF004 (class not partial) | Add `partial` modifier |
| FKF002 (method ignored in explicit mode) | Add `[ForgeMethod]` attribute |
| FKF300 (nested forging disabled) | Add `AllowNestedForging = true` to `[ForgeMethod]` |
| FKF109 (both [ForgeIgnore] and [ForgeMap]) | Remove `[ForgeMap]` |
| FKF112 (self-referencing [ForgeMap]) | Remove `[ForgeMap]` |
| FKF525 ([ForgeMethod] without [Forge] class) | Add `[Forge]` attribute to class |
| FKF526 ([ForgeConverter] without [Forge] class) | Add `[Forge]` attribute to class |

## Common Anti-Patterns

- Putting `[ForgeMap]` or `[ForgeIgnore]` on **source** type members — they only work on destination types (FKF527/FKF528).
- Using `[ForgeMethod]` without `[Forge]` on the class (FKF525).
- Expecting `AllowNestedForging` to work without a matching forge method in scope.
- Setting both `IgnoreIfNull` and `NullFallback` on the same member (FKF315).
- Forgetting `partial` on the class or method.
- Using `GenerateExpression = true` on update methods (FKF504).
